newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam plans revamp for troubled banks - paper.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam plans revamp for troubled banks - paper.

text.p: Vietnam's central bank plans to make cash-strapped private banks in Ho Chi Minh City take an injection of capital from state-owned companies, the Thanh Nien daily said in its March 20 edition.

"... the Ho Chi Minh City branch of the State Bank is asking the joint-stock commercial banks which do not have sufficient legal capital to increase state-owned enterprises' share in their capital to at least 10 percent," the paper said.
It added that if they failed to get a capital top-up from state firms, troubled banks would either be merged or converted to a People's Credit Fund.
Officials at the central State Bank of Vietnam this week declined to give any details of plans to protect the so-called joint-stock banks from persistent liquidity problems.
Rumours about the health of the country's 53 privately held banks, which sprang up during the past half-decade of tentative financial reform, have been circulating for weeks.
The daily Vietnam News this week quoted a State Bank report on overdue debt at banks in Ho Chi Minh City, the country's commercial hub.
It said "overdue debts of more than 12 months outstanding" were equivalent to 4.1 percent of all loans at state-owned commercial banks and 17.5 percent of the loan portfolio at joint-stock banks.
"Overdue debt" is a catch-all phrase which includes bad or non-performing debt, a Western concept not yet recognised in Vietnam.

Bankers say many of the banks ran into trouble after a flurry of deferred letter of credit deals for imports last year. Vietnam News said total bank guarantees through letters of credit in 1996 were estimated at $908 million.

The Joint-Stock Commercial Bank for Private Enterprises (VP Bank) has come under particular scrutiny after it had to extend the period of repayment under a letter of credit, though bankers say it is by no means the only bank to face such a situation.
